claims.statement: Allen said he had already paid each of his sureties $250 and would pay the whole debt if they gave him time.
Farrell sent for a Kentucky requisition and procured Allen's arrest after Allen refused his money demand.
Allen gave $2,000 bond (printed as $2°000) with Fred Walters and Jos. Schnaider as sureties.
Allen declared he would prosecute Farrell for attempted extortion.
Allen was arrested several days before 13 February 1884 at Farrell's instance, to await a Kentucky requisition.
Shortly before his arrest, W. J. Farrell wrote to Tom Allen demanding $200 and then appeared in person.
After a row with Tom Allen over more bond money, W. J. Farrell lodged a complaint that led to Allen's arrest.
Tom Allen was arrested on Saturday evening, 9 February 1884, at the instance of W. P. Farrell of Covington, Ky.
Farrell charged that Allen was wanted to answer an indictment in Kentucky.
Tom Allen was arrested at his saloon on Market Street, between Sixth and Seventh streets, on February 9, 1884, as a fugitive from Kentucky justice.
Tom Allen gave a $2,000 bond, with Joseph M. Schnaider and Frederick Watkins as securities, to appear before Judge Noonan the next day.
Judge Chester H. Krum, Thomas Morris and Frank Turner represented Tom Allen.
At the 13 February hearing Allen's side argued that Farrell's proceedings were simply an attempt to collect a debt.
Judge Noonan released Allen from custody, saying the case would never have been instituted had the money been paid.
After hearing both sides, the Prosecuting Attorney said he would not press the matter against Allen.
Judge Chester H. Krum asked Gov. Crittenden of Missouri to refuse to surrender Tom Allen on Kentucky's requisition.
Krum argued the requisition was meant to enforce collection of a debt Allen owed to Farrell, the bearer of the requisition.
Gov. Crittenden said he was not prepared to honor the Kentucky requisition for Allen and would consider it well first.
The paper judged that Allen would not be turned over or sent back to Kentucky.
Frank Rush was shot in front of Allen's saloon at 621 Market Street at about 1 a.m. on 22 December 1884 by an unknown man who escaped.
Tom Allen was the first of the prize-fight suspects arrested under the Franklin County warrants, a few minutes before noon on 1888-04-18.
Tom Allen, Flint's second, was named in a warrant charging him with aiding and abetting the McManus-Flint prize fight, a felony.
Tom Allen was captured at his saloon by the Franklin County officers and taken to the Four Courts on 1888-04-18.
Allen gave a $500 bond to appear before Justice Frazee at Union, Franklin County, at 10 o'clock the next morning.
Tom Allen was indicted by the Franklin County grand jury in connection with the Flint-McManus fight.
Tom Allen renewed his bond before Judge Noonan on May 19, 1888, after his indictment.
Tom Allen and Charley Daly were taken to the station after the street fight and gave bond.
Tom Allen and Charley Daly were taken to the Chestnut Street police station and released on bond.
The Police Court case against Tom Allen was continued until Thursday at Allen's request.
Tom Allen, Charley Daly and John Ryan were tried in Police Court on counter charges of disturbing the peace over the Sunday-morning street fight.
Judge Cady fined Tom Allen $10 for disturbing the peace.
Judge Cady fined John Ryan $15 on Tom Allen's charge of malicious trespass.
Allen's second count said Bill Clark received a sum printed as $75) from the Globe Printing Co. for Allen and had not paid it.
Tom Allen filed suit against Bill Clark, the final stakeholder in the Daly-McManus match.
Allen's petition asked for judgment for $1,000 he had deposited with the stakeholder, with interest and costs.
A St. Louis County warrant for prize-fighting, issued by Justice Caffrey, named Tom Allen among those charged for their part in the Kelly-McManus fight at Florissant.
Tom Allen was arrested on the afternoon of 11 February 1889 and gave bond.
Tom Allen, Tom Kelly and Dan Daly became bondsmen for all the defendants in the Lincoln County prize fight case at Troy.
Each defendant in the Lincoln County prize fight case was held in a $500 bond for his appearance.
N. C. Dryden of Troy and Mr. Boe of St. Louis were the lawyers for the defendants, as printed in the text.
Sheriff Jessie Coomes of Lincoln County, Mo., came to St. Louis seeking the arrest of Tom Allen and others on charges of prize fighting and abetting a fight.
The sheriff's arrest papers for Tom Allen and the others appeared to be defective, so he returned to Troy to have them perfected.
Tom Allen and the others were arrested in St. Louis about a week earlier by Detectives Burke and Fitzgerald, at the request of Lincoln County authorities.
The case against Tom Allen and the others was expected to go to trial in Lincoln County on the afternoon of September 16, 1889.
James St. John reported his watch and chain stolen and Tom Allen notified police, who took a description of two men.
Thomas Barrett and George Ohls were arrested on a corner near Allen's saloon after the watch was stolen.
A warrant charging Thomas Barrett with petit larceny was sworn out after St. John identified his watch.
Edward Reilly said Tom Allen, a saloon-keeper and prize-fighter on Market street, slugged him without provocation, leaving him with severe head injuries.
John Craig, an Irishman, was charged in the First District Police Court with disturbing Tom Allen's peace.
Judge Morris discharged Craig because a man who had disturbed Allen's peace could not have come out with a face as badly beaten as Craig's.
Tom Allen said he would try to get bail bonds for the jailed Sharpe and was willing to put up a cash guarantee.
Police arrested a suspect calling himself John Foley at Tom Allen's saloon on Market Street, St. Louis, after a witness pointed him out as one of the robbers of a Broadway saloon.
Patrick Sullivan and Charles Dempsey picked a fight with Tom Allen in his saloon on Tuesday night, and were left badly bruised in the Dispensary.
At about 1 a.m. Tom Allen fired three shots into the air from the sidewalk outside his saloon to get rid of two quarrelsome men, and no policeman was near.
Judge Peabody fined Patrick Sullivan $200 and Charles Dempsey $50 (printed as 3530) on Thursday morning for disturbing the peace.
Tom Allen was assaulted at his place, 619 Market street, at 2:30 Friday morning.
Two men jumped onto Tom Allen and one revolver shot was fired.
Robert Flannigan and Edward Clancy followed an unknown man out of Allen's place and tried to hold him up at a corner of Market street.
Police arrested Robert Flannigan and Edward Clancy, who were sent to Police Court.
